title: The "AI" Badge Doesn't Measure What You Think It Does
excerpt: Anthropic signed the EU AI Act's Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content, and...
content_html:
Anthropic signed the EU AI Act's Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content, and started marking text produced by Claude with an invisible statistical watermark. Within days, the same event got read two completely different ways on my feed.

The first reading, on dev.to, is by @sylwia-lask

She actually went and read the official documentation and reported what Anthropic really says: the watermark doesn't prove a text was entirely AI-generated – you can write something yourself, have Claude correct it or translate it, and it can still carry the mark. The reverse holds too: no watermark detected doesn't prove a human wrote everything.

The second, on Medium, called the announcement a "nuclear bomb" for the AI-generation community, and claimed "you are effectively carrying a digital scarlet letter." No citation of the actual documentation. Just outrage, with the appropriate amount of dramatic punctuation.

Between the two, I left a comment under Sylwia's article. Written in French, translated by ChatGPT, signed off with a question: how do you classify a text thought through, written, and reviewed by a human, but whose final English phrasing came out of a model? It wasn't a rhetorical question. I still don't have an answer.

Three things people keep conflating

The Medium article mixes together, without ever saying so, three mechanisms that have almost nothing to do with each other.

Anthropic's watermark. A statistical signal baked into the model, documented, which openly acknowledges its own limits: it can disappear after enough editing or translation, and its presence says nothing about who came up with the idea in the first place.

Third-party consumer detectors. ZeroGPT and its relatives. Tools that have existed for years, unrelated to Anthropic, whose reliability has never been seriously demonstrated at scale.

Platform decisions. A badge displayed on Medium, a curation algorithm that penalizes flagged content. These are editorial choices specific to each platform, not a mechanical consequence of the watermark.

The Medium article writes as though the first link automatically triggers the next two: Anthropic marks, so detectors will catch everything, so platforms will punish. The reasoning collapses the moment you separate the links – and for good reason: detecting that a model was involved in producing a text is not the same as determining that the text was "written by AI." That conflation hides a deeper one, which public debate almost systematically ignores.

Assisted, generated, produced: three different verbs

A text assisted by AI stays under human editorial control from start to finish: the idea, the angle, the structure, and the final decision to publish belong to someone, no matter how many back-and-forths with a model happened along the way to correct, rephrase, translate, or pressure-test a line of reasoning. A text generated by AI comes out of a prompt, without that upstream control – the idea itself came from the human, but the generated text, as it stands, belongs to the model. A text produced by AI at industrial scale is something else again: an automated publishing pipeline, without anything resembling editorial oversight.

What separates the three, then, isn't how much the model intervened – it's who kept their hand on the decisions.

These three cases carry entirely different editorial responsibility. Treating them as a single category ("AI content") means judging a text on a binary criterion where the reality is a full spectrum of nuance – which is exactly what an undifferentiated "processed by AI" badge does.

What an actual test shows

I ran an article I wrote in April 2021 – before any consumer-facing LLM existed – through ZeroGPT. A test about a year ago gave it a 97% AI probability. A recent test, on the exact same text, with the exact same tool, gives 8.6%.

Same tool. Same text, down to the punctuation. Two incompatible scores, a year apart.

Digging into the flagged passages in the second test, a pattern emerges. These aren't random sentences: they're consistently the most neutral, most pedagogical, most well-structured passages in the piece – a definition of what a web server is, an explanation of CentOS Stream, a step-by-step automated update procedure. The passages where my voice actually comes through – the self-deprecation, the verbal tics, the Neapolitan moka pot bought at a flea market – are never flagged.

One test doesn't prove what a detection model measures in general. But this one strongly suggests the tool reacts to stylistic neutrality and structural regularity, not to a text's actual origin. Which is precisely the problem: those characteristics existed in human writing long before LLMs did. The detector is chasing a style whose origin is human, using the machine's imitation of it as the reference point. The reasoning eats its own tail.

How this piece was actually made

Since the whole point of this article is how hard it is to judge a text by its origin rather than its content, it's worth being transparent about how this one was produced.

The starting point wasn't this article: it was a comment under a Medium post that annoyed me enough to reply. From there, several hours of back-and-forth with Claude – not to have it write for me, but to pressure-test angles, check numbers, and go dig up original sources instead of relying on my own fuzzy memory. The ZeroGPT test wasn't improvised for the article, either: I reran it to verify what I was recalling from memory, and the result changed the conclusion I was about to draw.

First draft written in French – the language I actually think in. Several rounds of review, cross-checked across a few different AI models – ChatGPT, Kimi, Grok, Mistral – to catch inconsistencies and spots where the argument went soft. I then read and corrected it myself, outside of Claude (I use NotepadMD), because I never let a text out the door without going through it line by line. Translation into English after that, then a review of that translation, because a lexically faithful translation can still betray the tone if nobody checks it.

By the end of this process, the text probably carries a watermark. It also took up several hours of research, verification, and both automated and human review – and my own review isn't the least of it: after every rewrite, and again at the end of the process. Both facts are true at the same time, and no detector will ever be able to tell them apart.

What a badge actually costs

Everything above is a technical demonstration. It says nothing about what happens once the text is published, and that might be the more important part.

A "processed by AI" badge, applied without distinguishing assisted, generated, and produced, puts an author who spent hours thinking, checking, and writing in the same bucket as a content farm publishing a hundred articles a day with no human oversight. A rushed reader doesn't see the nuance – they see the badge, and file the thinking author under "cheater." That's a real loss for someone who never cheated: their work gets judged on a signal that measures neither the effort nor the actual editorial control behind it, only whether a tool showed up somewhere in the chain.

And that loss has an absurd mirror image. The same readers who reject an article marked "AI" accept, without blinking, the AI-generated summary sitting at the top of their Google search results – without reading it critically, without checking the sources it pulled from, and most often without ever clicking through to the original article. Independent studies converge on this: when an AI summary appears in a Google search, clicks to third-party sites drop by half, sometimes more, depending on methodology. In other words, the reader who calls an article "AI slop" over a badge probably let an AI summarize ten other topics for them that same week, without ever checking what it kept or what it distorted. AI isn't rejected on principle. It's rejected when it's visible and claimed, and accepted when it's invisible and imposed by default.

This shift from click to summary is also a broader loss of reading, independent of any badge: a full article, nuanced, sometimes contradictory, replaced by three smoothed-over lines nobody ever questions. The reader loses the friction that would have forced them to evaluate a source, a line of reasoning, a style – exactly what the badge claims to let people judge, and what the summary skips without any debate at all.

What this doesn't fix

None of this will stop an "AI slop" comment under this piece. I've never gotten one on dev.to. On Reddit, I have.

But look at who tends to write that kind of comment. Rarely people genuinely engaging with the topic. Often people chasing the buzz of a word that lands. On Reddit, the accounts behind these comments often show a broader pattern of reflexive, repeated downvoting across unrelated posts – a signal of rejection that has little to do with the content actually in front of them.

The technical demonstration and the social judgment are two different things, and the second doesn't get talked out of itself by the first. "AI slop" has stopped being a judgment about a text at all: it's become a blunt, reflexive rejection signal people display, regardless of whether they read anything.

If the badge doesn't measure origin, and social judgment doesn't care about the measurement, maybe the question worth asking isn't "who wrote this" but "who thought this through."

The nuance matters here. In the process I just described, the initiative never changed hands: I'm the one who opens the session, sets the topic, decides whether an angle holds up or needs to be dropped. A model doesn't come looking for me with an idea I didn't already have. And if it writes a paragraph I didn't ask for, it goes in the trash – which is perfectly observable in what I keep and what I discard from one session to the next.

Who thought through the initial disagreement with the Medium piece, and chose to separate watermark, detector, and platform instead of treating them as one thing? Who decided a test was worth more than an opinion, and reran it twice instead of republishing a fuzzy memory?

Those are questions I can answer, text by text, decision by decision. No detector asks them. It looks at the final shape and infers an origin from it – when the origin was never in the shape. It was in the chain of decisions that came before it.

blocks.html_en: I ran an article I wrote in April 2021 – before any consumer-facing LLM existed – through ZeroGPT. A test about a year ago gave it a 97% AI probability. A recent test, on the exact same text, with the exact same tool, gives 8.6%.

sentences.en: I ran an article I wrote in April 2021 – before any consumer-facing LLM existed – through ZeroGPT.
sentences.zh: 我通过 ZeroGPT 发表了一篇我在 2021 年 4 月写的文章——在任何面向消费者的法学硕士存在之前。

sentences.en: A test about a year ago gave it a 97% AI probability.
sentences.zh: 大约一年前的一次测试给出了 97% 的 AI 概率。

sentences.en: A recent test, on the exact same text, with the exact same tool, gives 8.6%.
sentences.zh: 最近使用完全相同的工具对完全相同的文本进行的测试给出了 8.6%。

blocks.html_en: Same tool. Same text, down to the punctuation. Two incompatible scores, a year apart.

sentences.en: Same tool.
sentences.zh: 相同的工具。

sentences.en: Same text, down to the punctuation.
sentences.zh: 相同的文字，连标点符号都没有。

sentences.en: Two incompatible scores, a year apart.
sentences.zh: 两个不相容的分数，相差一年。

blocks.html_en: Digging into the flagged passages in the second test, a pattern emerges. These aren't random sentences: they're consistently the most neutral, most pedagogical, most well-structured passages in the piece – a definition of what a web server is, an explanation of CentOS Stream, a step-by-step automated update procedure. The passages where my voice actually comes through – the self-deprecation, the verbal tics, the Neapolitan moka pot bought at a flea market – are never flagged.

sentences.en: Digging into the flagged passages in the second test, a pattern emerges.
sentences.zh: 深入研究第二次测试中标记的段落，就会发现一种模式。

sentences.en: These aren't random sentences: they're consistently the most neutral, most pedagogical, most well-structured passages in the piece – a definition of what a web server is, an explanation of CentOS Stream, a step-by-step automated update procedure.
sentences.zh: 这些不是随意的句子：它们始终是本文中最中立、最具教学性、结构最完善的段落——Web 服务器的定义、CentOS Stream 的解释、逐步的自动更新过程。

sentences.en: The passages where my voice actually comes through – the self-deprecation, the verbal tics, the Neapolitan moka pot bought at a flea market – are never flagged.
sentences.zh: 我的声音真正出现的段落——自嘲、言语抽搐、在跳蚤市场买的那不勒斯摩卡壶——从来没有被标记过。

blocks.html_en: One test doesn't prove what a detection model measures in general. But this one strongly suggests the tool reacts to stylistic neutrality and structural regularity, not to a text's actual origin. Which is precisely the problem: those characteristics existed in human writing long before LLMs did. The detector is chasing a style whose origin is human, using the machine's imitation of it as the reference point. The reasoning eats its own tail.

sentences.en: One test doesn't prove what a detection model measures in general.
sentences.zh: 一项测试并不能证明检测模型的总体测量结果。

sentences.en: But this one strongly suggests the tool reacts to stylistic neutrality and structural regularity, not to a text's actual origin.
sentences.zh: 但这强烈表明该工具对文体中立性和结构规律性做出反应，而不是对文本的实际起源做出反应。

sentences.en: Which is precisely the problem: those characteristics existed in human writing long before LLMs did.
sentences.zh: 这正是问题所在：这些特征早在法学硕士出现之前就已经存在于人类写作中。

sentences.en: The detector is chasing a style whose origin is human, using the machine's imitation of it as the reference point.
sentences.zh: 探测器正在追寻一种源于人类的风格，以机器对它的模仿作为参考点。

sentences.en: The reasoning eats its own tail.
sentences.zh: 推理自食其果。

blocks.html_en: How this piece was actually made

sentences.en: How this piece was actually made
sentences.zh: 这件作品实际上是如何制作的

blocks.html_en: Since the whole point of this article is how hard it is to judge a text by its origin rather than its content, it's worth being transparent about how this one was produced.

sentences.en: Since the whole point of this article is how hard it is to judge a text by its origin rather than its content, it's worth being transparent about how this one was produced.
sentences.zh: 由于本文的重点是根据文本的来源而不是内容来判断文本是多么困难，因此值得对这篇文章的制作方式保持透明。

blocks.html_en: The starting point wasn't this article: it was a comment under a Medium post that annoyed me enough to reply. From there, several hours of back-and-forth with Claude – not to have it write for me, but to pressure-test angles, check numbers, and go dig up original sources instead of relying on my own fuzzy memory. The ZeroGPT test wasn't improvised for the article, either: I reran it to verify what I was recalling from memory, and the result changed the conclusion I was about to draw.

sentences.en: The starting point wasn't this article: it was a comment under a Medium post that annoyed me enough to reply.
sentences.zh: 出发点不是这篇文章：这是一篇 Medium 帖子下的一条评论，让我很恼火，所以才回复。

sentences.en: From there, several hours of back-and-forth with Claude – not to have it write for me, but to pressure-test angles, check numbers, and go dig up original sources instead of relying on my own fuzzy memory.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，我与克劳德进行了几个小时的来回交流——不是让它为我写，而是对角度进行压力测试，检查数字，并挖掘原始资料，而不是依赖我自己的模糊记忆。

sentences.en: The ZeroGPT test wasn't improvised for the article, either: I reran it to verify what I was recalling from memory, and the result changed the conclusion I was about to draw.
sentences.zh: ZeroGPT 测试也不是为这篇文章临时准备的：我重新运行它来验证我从记忆中回忆的内容，结果改变了我即将得出的结论。

blocks.html_en: First draft written in French – the language I actually think in. Several rounds of review, cross-checked across a few different AI models – ChatGPT, Kimi, Grok, Mistral – to catch inconsistencies and spots where the argument went soft. I then read and corrected it myself, outside of Claude (I use NotepadMD), because I never let a text out the door without going through it line by line. Translation into English after that, then a review of that translation, because a lexically faithful translation can still betray the tone if nobody checks it.

sentences.en: First draft written in French – the language I actually think in.
sentences.zh: 第一份草稿是用法语写的——我实际上用的是法语。

sentences.en: Several rounds of review, cross-checked across a few different AI models – ChatGPT, Kimi, Grok, Mistral – to catch inconsistencies and spots where the argument went soft.
sentences.zh: 经过几轮审查，对几个不同的人工智能模型（ChatGPT、Kimi、Grok、Mistral）进行交叉检查，以发现不一致之处和争论变得软弱的地方。

sentences.en: I then read and corrected it myself, outside of Claude (I use NotepadMD), because I never let a text out the door without going through it line by line.
sentences.zh: 然后，我在 Claude 之外（我使用 NotepadMD）自己阅读并更正它，因为我从来不会在没有逐行浏览的情况下将文本放出门外。

sentences.en: Translation into English after that, then a review of that translation, because a lexically faithful translation can still betray the tone if nobody checks it.
sentences.zh: 之后翻译成英文，然后对该翻译进行审查，因为如果没有人检查，词汇忠实的翻译仍然可能会泄露语气。

blocks.html_en: By the end of this process, the text probably carries a watermark. It also took up several hours of research, verification, and both automated and human review – and my own review isn't the least of it: after every rewrite, and again at the end of the process. Both facts are true at the same time, and no detector will ever be able to tell them apart.

sentences.en: By the end of this process, the text probably carries a watermark.
sentences.zh: 在此过程结束时，文本可能带有水印。

sentences.en: It also took up several hours of research, verification, and both automated and human review – and my own review isn't the least of it: after every rewrite, and again at the end of the process.
sentences.zh: 它还花费了几个小时的研究、验证以及自动和人工审查——而我自己的审查并不是最不重要的：在每次重写之后，以及在过程结束时再次进行。

sentences.en: Both facts are true at the same time, and no detector will ever be able to tell them apart.
sentences.zh: 这两个事实同时成立，任何探测器都无法区分它们。

blocks.html_en: What a badge actually costs

sentences.en: What a badge actually costs
sentences.zh: 徽章的实际成本是多少

blocks.html_en: Everything above is a technical demonstration. It says nothing about what happens once the text is published, and that might be the more important part.

sentences.en: Everything above is a technical demonstration.
sentences.zh: 以上都是技术演示。

sentences.en: It says nothing about what happens once the text is published, and that might be the more important part.
sentences.zh: 它没有提及文本发布后会发生什么，而这可能是更重要的部分。

blocks.html_en: A "processed by AI" badge, applied without distinguishing assisted, generated, and produced, puts an author who spent hours thinking, checking, and writing in the same bucket as a content farm publishing a hundred articles a day with no human oversight. A rushed reader doesn't see the nuance – they see the badge, and file the thinking author under "cheater." That's a real loss for someone who never cheated: their work gets judged on a signal that measures neither the effort nor the actual editorial control behind it, only whether a tool showed up somewhere in the chain.

sentences.en: A "processed by AI" badge, applied without distinguishing assisted, generated, and produced, puts an author who spent hours thinking, checking, and writing in the same bucket as a content farm publishing a hundred articles a day with no human oversight.
sentences.zh: 一个“由人工智能处理”的徽章，在不区分辅助、生成和制作的情况下使用，将花费数小时思考、检查和写作的作者与每天在没有人工监督的情况下发布一百篇文章的内容农场放在同一个桶中。

sentences.en: A rushed reader doesn't see the nuance – they see the badge, and file the thinking author under "cheater."
sentences.zh: 匆忙的读者看不到其中的细微差别——他们看到了徽章，并将有思想的作者归入“骗子”之下。

sentences.en: That's a real loss for someone who never cheated: their work gets judged on a signal that measures neither the effort nor the actual editorial control behind it, only whether a tool showed up somewhere in the chain.
sentences.zh: 对于从不作弊的人来说，这是一个真正的损失：他们的工作是根据一个信号来评判的，这个信号既不衡量其努力程度，也不衡量其背后的实际编辑控制，只衡量工具是否出现在链条中的某个地方。

blocks.html_en: And that loss has an absurd mirror image. The same readers who reject an article marked "AI" accept, without blinking, the AI-generated summary sitting at the top of their Google search results – without reading it critically, without checking the sources it pulled from, and most often without ever clicking through to the original article. Independent studies converge on this: when an AI summary appears in a Google search, clicks to third-party sites drop by half, sometimes more, depending on methodology. In other words, the reader who calls an article "AI slop" over a badge probably let an AI summarize ten other topics for them that same week, without ever checking what it kept or what it distorted. AI isn't rejected on principle. It's rejected when it's visible and claimed, and accepted when it's invisible and imposed by default.

sentences.en: And that loss has an absurd mirror image.
sentences.zh: 这种损失有一个荒谬的镜像。

sentences.en: The same readers who reject an article marked "AI" accept, without blinking, the AI-generated summary sitting at the top of their Google search results – without reading it critically, without checking the sources it pulled from, and most often without ever clicking through to the original article.
sentences.zh: 那些拒绝标记为“人工智能”的文章的读者，眼睛也不眨一下，就接受了位于谷歌搜索结果顶部的人工智能生成的摘要——没有批判性地阅读它，没有检查它的来源，而且最常见的是没有点击查看原始文章。

sentences.en: Independent studies converge on this: when an AI summary appears in a Google search, clicks to third-party sites drop by half, sometimes more, depending on methodology.
sentences.zh: 独立研究集中在这一点上：当人工智能摘要出现在谷歌搜索中时，第三方网站的点击量会下降一半，有时甚至更多，具体取决于方法。

sentences.en: In other words, the reader who calls an article "AI slop" over a badge probably let an AI summarize ten other topics for them that same week, without ever checking what it kept or what it distorted.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，那些将一篇文章称为“AI slop”而不是徽章的读者可能会让人工智能在同一周为他们总结其他十个主题，而不会检查它保留了什么或歪曲了什么。

sentences.en: AI isn't rejected on principle.
sentences.zh: 原则上人工智能并没有被拒绝。

sentences.en: It's rejected when it's visible and claimed, and accepted when it's invisible and imposed by default.
sentences.zh: 当它可见并声明时，它会被拒绝；当它不可见并默认强加时，它会被接受。

blocks.html_en: This shift from click to summary is also a broader loss of reading, independent of any badge: a full article, nuanced, sometimes contradictory, replaced by three smoothed-over lines nobody ever questions. The reader loses the friction that would have forced them to evaluate a source, a line of reasoning, a style – exactly what the badge claims to let people judge, and what the summary skips without any debate at all.

sentences.en: This shift from click to summary is also a broader loss of reading, independent of any badge: a full article, nuanced, sometimes contradictory, replaced by three smoothed-over lines nobody ever questions.
sentences.zh: 这种从点击到摘要的转变也是一种更广泛的阅读损失，与任何徽章无关：一篇完整的文章，细致入微，有时甚至是矛盾的，被三行平滑的线条所取代，没有人质疑。

sentences.en: The reader loses the friction that would have forced them to evaluate a source, a line of reasoning, a style – exactly what the badge claims to let people judge, and what the summary skips without any debate at all.
sentences.zh: 读者不再会被迫评估来源、推理路线、风格——正是徽章声称让人们判断的东西，以及摘要在没有任何辩论的情况下跳过的东西。

blocks.html_en: What this doesn't fix

sentences.en: What this doesn't fix
sentences.zh: 这不能解决什么问题

blocks.html_en: None of this will stop an "AI slop" comment under this piece. I've never gotten one on dev.to. On Reddit, I have.

sentences.en: None of this will stop an "AI slop" comment under this piece.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都无法阻止这篇文章下的“AI slop”评论。

sentences.en: I've never gotten one on dev.to.
sentences.zh: 我从来没有在 dev.to 上得到过一个。

sentences.en: On Reddit, I have.
sentences.zh: 在 Reddit 上，我有。

blocks.html_en: But look at who tends to write that kind of comment. Rarely people genuinely engaging with the topic. Often people chasing the buzz of a word that lands. On Reddit, the accounts behind these comments often show a broader pattern of reflexive, repeated downvoting across unrelated posts – a signal of rejection that has little to do with the content actually in front of them.

sentences.en: But look at who tends to write that kind of comment.
sentences.zh: 但看看谁倾向于写这种评论。

sentences.en: Rarely people genuinely engaging with the topic.
sentences.zh: 很少有人真正参与这个话题。

sentences.en: Often people chasing the buzz of a word that lands.
sentences.zh: 人们常常追逐某个词的流行。

sentences.en: On Reddit, the accounts behind these comments often show a broader pattern of reflexive, repeated downvoting across unrelated posts – a signal of rejection that has little to do with the content actually in front of them.
sentences.zh: 在 Reddit 上，这些评论背后的账户通常会表现出一种更广泛的模式，即对不相关的帖子进行反射性、反复的否决——这是一种拒绝的信号，与他们面前的实际内容无关。

blocks.html_en: The technical demonstration and the social judgment are two different things, and the second doesn't get talked out of itself by the first. "AI slop" has stopped being a judgment about a text at all: it's become a blunt, reflexive rejection signal people display, regardless of whether they read anything.

sentences.en: The technical demonstration and the social judgment are two different things, and the second doesn't get talked out of itself by the first.
sentences.zh: 技术论证和社会判断是两件不同的事情，而后者并不能被前者所取代。

sentences.en: "AI slop" has stopped being a judgment about a text at all: it's become a blunt, reflexive rejection signal people display, regardless of whether they read anything.
sentences.zh: “AI slop”已经不再是对文本的判断：它已经成为人们表现出的一种生硬的、本能的拒绝信号，无论他们是否阅读了任何内容。

blocks.html_en: If the badge doesn't measure origin, and social judgment doesn't care about the measurement, maybe the question worth asking isn't "who wrote this" but "who thought this through."

sentences.en: If the badge doesn't measure origin, and social judgment doesn't care about the measurement, maybe the question worth asking isn't "who wrote this" but "who thought this through."
sentences.zh: 如果徽章不衡量起源，而社会判断也不关心衡量标准，那么也许值得问的问题不是“谁写了这个”，而是“谁想通了这个”。

blocks.html_en: The nuance matters here. In the process I just described, the initiative never changed hands: I'm the one who opens the session, sets the topic, decides whether an angle holds up or needs to be dropped. A model doesn't come looking for me with an idea I didn't already have. And if it writes a paragraph I didn't ask for, it goes in the trash – which is perfectly observable in what I keep and what I discard from one session to the next.

sentences.en: The nuance matters here.
sentences.zh: 这里的细微差别很重要。

sentences.en: In the process I just described, the initiative never changed hands: I'm the one who opens the session, sets the topic, decides whether an angle holds up or needs to be dropped.
sentences.zh: 在我刚才描述的过程中，倡议从未易手：我是发起会议、设定主题、决定某个角度是否成立或需要放弃的人。

sentences.en: A model doesn't come looking for me with an idea I didn't already have.
sentences.zh: 模特不会带着我还没有的想法来找我。

sentences.en: And if it writes a paragraph I didn't ask for, it goes in the trash – which is perfectly observable in what I keep and what I discard from one session to the next.
sentences.zh: 如果它写了一段我没有要求的段落，它就会被扔进垃圾桶——这在我从一个会话到下一个会话中保留的内容和丢弃的内容中完全可以观察到。

blocks.html_en: Who thought through the initial disagreement with the Medium piece, and chose to separate watermark, detector, and platform instead of treating them as one thing? Who decided a test was worth more than an opinion, and reran it twice instead of republishing a fuzzy memory?

sentences.en: Who thought through the initial disagreement with the Medium piece, and chose to separate watermark, detector, and platform instead of treating them as one thing?
sentences.zh: 谁仔细考虑了最初与 Medium 文章的分歧，并选择将水印、检测器和平台分开，而不是将它们视为一件事？

sentences.en: Who decided a test was worth more than an opinion, and reran it twice instead of republishing a fuzzy memory?
sentences.zh: 谁认为测试比意见更有价值，并重新运行两次而不是重新发布模糊的记忆？

blocks.html_en: Those are questions I can answer, text by text, decision by decision. No detector asks them. It looks at the final shape and infers an origin from it – when the origin was never in the shape. It was in the chain of decisions that came before it.

sentences.en: Those are questions I can answer, text by text, decision by decision.
sentences.zh: 这些是我可以逐条回答、逐个决定回答的问题。

sentences.en: No detector asks them.
sentences.zh: 没有探测器询问他们。

sentences.en: It looks at the final shape and infers an origin from it – when the origin was never in the shape.
sentences.zh: 它着眼于最终的形状并从中推断出原点——而原点从来不在形状中。

sentences.en: It was in the chain of decisions that came before it.
sentences.zh: 这是在它之前的一系列决策中。

content_html_zh:
Anthropic 签署了《欧盟人工智能法案关于人工智能生成内容透明度的行为准则》，并开始使用不可见的统计水印标记克劳德生成的文本。 几天之内，同一事件在我的提要上以两种完全不同的方式被阅读。

dev.to 上的第一篇阅读由 @sylwia-lask 撰写

她实际上去阅读了官方文档，并报告了 Anthropic 真正所说的内容：水印并不能证明文本完全是人工智能生成的——你可以自己写一些东西，让克劳德纠正或翻译它，它仍然可以带有标记。 反之亦然：没有检测到水印并不能证明所有内容都是人写的。

第二个是在 Medium 上发布的，称这一公告是人工智能一代社区的“核弹”，并声称“你实际上携带着一个数字红字”。 没有引用实际文档。 只是愤怒，并带有适当数量的戏剧性标点符号。

两人之间，我在Sylwia的文章下留下了评论。 用法语撰写，由 ChatGPT 翻译，最后提出一个问题：如何对由人类思考、编写和审阅的文本进行分类，但其最终的英语措辞来自模型？ 这不是一个反问句。 我仍然没有答案。

人们总是混淆三件事

Medium 上的文章将三种几乎毫无关系的机制混合在一起，但从未明言。

人类的水印。 模型中融入了统计信号并记录下来，它公开承认自己的局限性：经过足够的编辑或翻译后，它可能会消失，而且它的存在并不能说明是谁首先提出了这个想法。

第三方消费者探测器。 ZeroGPT 及其亲属。 这些工具已经存在多年，与 Anthropic 无关，其可靠性从未得到大规模的认真证明。

平台决策。 Medium 上显示的徽章，这是一种惩罚标记内容的管理算法。 这些是针对每个平台的编辑选择，而不是水印的机械结果。

Medium 文章写道，好像第一个链接会自动触发接下来的两个链接：人为标记，因此探测器会捕获一切，因此平台会惩罚。 一旦你分开链接，推理就崩溃了——而且有充分的理由：检测模型参与生成文本与确定文本是“由人工智能编写”不同。 这种合并隐藏了更深层次的问题，而公共辩论几乎系统性地忽视了这一问题。

协助、生成、产生：三个不同的动词

人工智能辅助的文本从头到尾都处于人类编辑控制之下：想法、角度、结构和最终的发布决定都属于某人，无论在纠正、改写、翻译或压力测试推理过程中与模型发生了多少次来回。 人工智能生成的文本是根据提示生成的，没有上游控制——想法本身来自人类，但生成的文本就其本身而言属于模型。 人工智能在工业规模上生成的文本又是另一回事：一条自动化的出版管道，没有任何类似编辑监督的东西。

那么，这三者的区别不在于模型干预的程度，而在于谁掌控着决策。

这三个案例承担着完全不同的编辑责任。 将它们视为单一类别（“人工智能内容”）意味着根据二元标准来判断文本，其中现实是全方位的细微差别 - 这正是无差别的“由人工智能处理”徽章所做的。

实际测试表明什么

我通过 ZeroGPT 发表了一篇我在 2021 年 4 月写的文章——在任何面向消费者的法学硕士存在之前。 大约一年前的一次测试给出了 97% 的 AI 概率。 最近使用完全相同的工具对完全相同的文本进行的测试给出了 8.6%。

相同的工具。 相同的文字，连标点符号都没有。 两个不相容的分数，相差一年。

深入研究第二次测试中标记的段落，就会发现一种模式。 这些不是随意的句子：它们始终是本文中最中立、最具教学性、结构最完善的段落——Web 服务器的定义、CentOS Stream 的解释、逐步的自动更新过程。 我的声音真正出现的段落——自嘲、言语抽搐、在跳蚤市场买的那不勒斯摩卡壶——从来没有被标记过。

一项测试并不能证明检测模型的总体测量结果。 但这强烈表明该工具对文体中立性和结构规律性做出反应，而不是对文本的实际起源做出反应。 这正是问题所在：这些特征早在法学硕士出现之前就已经存在于人类写作中。 探测器正在追寻一种源于人类的风格，以机器对它的模仿作为参考点。 推理自食其果。

这件作品实际上是如何制作的

由于本文的重点是根据文本的来源而不是内容来判断文本是多么困难，因此值得对这篇文章的制作方式保持透明。

出发点不是这篇文章：这是一篇 Medium 帖子下的一条评论，让我很恼火，所以才回复。 从那时起，我与克劳德进行了几个小时的来回交流——不是让它为我写，而是对角度进行压力测试，检查数字，并挖掘原始资料，而不是依赖我自己的模糊记忆。 ZeroGPT 测试也不是为这篇文章临时准备的：我重新运行它来验证我从记忆中回忆的内容，结果改变了我即将得出的结论。

第一份草稿是用法语写的——我实际上用的是法语。 经过几轮审查，对几个不同的人工智能模型（ChatGPT、Kimi、Grok、Mistral）进行交叉检查，以发现不一致之处和争论变得软弱的地方。 然后，我在 Claude 之外（我使用 NotepadMD）自己阅读并更正它，因为我从来不会在没有逐行浏览的情况下将文本放出门外。 之后翻译成英文，然后对该翻译进行审查，因为如果没有人检查，词汇忠实的翻译仍然可能会泄露语气。

在此过程结束时，文本可能带有水印。 它还花费了几个小时的研究、验证以及自动和人工审查——而我自己的审查并不是最不重要的：在每次重写之后，以及在过程结束时再次进行。 这两个事实同时成立，任何探测器都无法区分它们。

徽章的实际成本是多少

以上都是技术演示。 它没有提及文本发布后会发生什么，而这可能是更重要的部分。

一个“由人工智能处理”的徽章，在不区分辅助、生成和制作的情况下使用，将花费数小时思考、检查和写作的作者与每天在没有人工监督的情况下发布一百篇文章的内容农场放在同一个桶中。 匆忙的读者看不到其中的细微差别——他们看到了徽章，并将有思想的作者归入“骗子”之下。 对于从不作弊的人来说，这是一个真正的损失：他们的工作是根据一个信号来评判的，这个信号既不衡量其努力程度，也不衡量其背后的实际编辑控制，只衡量工具是否出现在链条中的某个地方。

这种损失有一个荒谬的镜像。 那些拒绝标记为“人工智能”的文章的读者，眼睛也不眨一下，就接受了位于谷歌搜索结果顶部的人工智能生成的摘要——没有批判性地阅读它，没有检查它的来源，而且最常见的是没有点击查看原始文章。 独立研究集中在这一点上：当人工智能摘要出现在谷歌搜索中时，第三方网站的点击量会下降一半，有时甚至更多，具体取决于方法。 换句话说，那些将一篇文章称为“AI slop”而不是徽章的读者可能会让人工智能在同一周为他们总结其他十个主题，而不会检查它保留了什么或歪曲了什么。 原则上人工智能并没有被拒绝。 当它可见并声明时，它会被拒绝；当它不可见并默认强加时，它会被接受。

这种从点击到摘要的转变也是一种更广泛的阅读损失，与任何徽章无关：一篇完整的文章，细致入微，有时甚至是矛盾的，被三行平滑的线条所取代，没有人质疑。 读者不再会被迫评估来源、推理路线、风格——正是徽章声称让人们判断的东西，以及摘要在没有任何辩论的情况下跳过的东西。

这不能解决什么问题

所有这些都无法阻止这篇文章下的“AI slop”评论。 我从来没有在 dev.to 上得到过一个。 在 Reddit 上，我有。

但看看谁倾向于写这种评论。 很少有人真正参与这个话题。 人们常常追逐某个词的流行。 在 Reddit 上，这些评论背后的账户通常会表现出一种更广泛的模式，即对不相关的帖子进行反射性、反复的否决——这是一种拒绝的信号，与他们面前的实际内容无关。

技术论证和社会判断是两件不同的事情，而后者并不能被前者所取代。 “AI slop”已经不再是对文本的判断：它已经成为人们表现出的一种生硬的、本能的拒绝信号，无论他们是否阅读了任何内容。

如果徽章不衡量起源，而社会判断也不关心衡量标准，那么也许值得问的问题不是“谁写了这个”，而是“谁想通了这个”。

这里的细微差别很重要。 在我刚才描述的过程中，倡议从未易手：我是发起会议、设定主题、决定某个角度是否成立或需要放弃的人。 模特不会带着我还没有的想法来找我。 如果它写了一段我没有要求的段落，它就会被扔进垃圾桶——这在我从一个会话到下一个会话中保留的内容和丢弃的内容中完全可以观察到。

谁仔细考虑了最初与 Medium 文章的分歧，并选择将水印、检测器和平台分开，而不是将它们视为一件事？ 谁认为测试比意见更有价值，并重新运行两次而不是重新发布模糊的记忆？

这些是我可以逐条回答、逐个决定回答的问题。 没有探测器询问他们。 它着眼于最终的形状并从中推断出原点——而原点从来不在形状中。 这是在它之前的一系列决策中。
